sections.title: Global Film Theory
sections.description: This course will provide an introduction to some of the most important film theory debates and allow us to explore how writers and filmmakers from different countries and historical periods have attempted to make sense of the changing phenomenon known as "cinema," to think cinematically. Topics under consideration may include: spectatorship, authorship, the apparatus, sound, editing, realism, race, gender and sexuality, stardom, the culture industry, the nation and decolonization, what counts as film theory and what counts as cinema, and the challenges of considering film theory in a global context, including the challenge of working across languages. There will be an asynchronous weekly film screening for this course. No knowledge of film theory is presumed.

sections.title: The Global Film Theory Club
sections.description: This device-free, seminar-style discussion class seeks to cultivate a film club community as we grapple with some key contemporary film theory debates, framed within the context of recent interventions as well as earlier critiques that seek to challenge film theory’s geopolitical biases and blind spots. Together, we will examine how film theorists as well as filmmakers from different countries, communities, and (primarily) 21st century moments have attempted to make sense of the changing phenomenon known as “cinema,” to think cinematically. Topics under consideration include: spectatorship, authorship, the apparatus, translation and subtitles, archives and preservation, festivals, blockbusters and the popular, animation, corporeality, virtuality, the national / transnational / global, decolonization, and what “counts” as film and film theory in different contexts. No knowledge of film theory is presumed. In the first part of the 3-hour class we will watch a film or some short films together and develop skills for taking notes on your responses to films while watching, with the goal of thinking actively across theoretical texts and the shared film experience. In the second part of the class, we will work through the assigned texts together using a variety of approaches to build skills and confidence with reading, writing, talking about and contextualizing film theory and to deepen our collective understanding of the films we watch together.
